A convicted murderer moaned and complained of excruciating pain as he was put to death by lethal injection in Texas in an execution that took more than an hour, witnesses said. Reinaldo Dennes, 70, was executed at a state prison in Huntsville on Thursday evening for the 1996 murder of a diamond dealer during a robbery. Dennes was killed by the same drug — pentobarbital — that was used in the failed execution in Tennessee of another condemned murderer, Christa Pike, in September. Pike survived the attempted execution. She was hospitalized in critical condition but has since been returned to prison. Jeff Hood, Dennes’s spiritual adviser, who was in the execution chamber as he was being put to death, described it as a “botched” execution that took more than an hour. Michael Graczyk, a reporter with the US news agency The Associated Press who attended the execution, also said it was unusual. Graczyk said he has witnessed nearly 500 executions by lethal injection and Dennes’s was “dramatically different.” Vietnam scraps capital punishment for drug trafficking US monitors trial of Egyptian Christian convert facing death penalty Trial of man accused of killing Charlie Kirk set for June 2028 Dennes “moaned of excruciating pain” as he was injected with the lethal drugs, he said. Amanda Hernandez, spokeswoman for the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ), said there was initially some difficulty finding suitable veins for the IV needles that delivered the lethal drugs but denied the execution was botched. “TDCJ denies any claim of the execution being ‘botched,'” Hernandez said. “The agency followed all of its protocols and the execution was successfully carried out. “IVs were inserted into the most viable veins available, in the left foot and left side of the neck,” she said. “Dennes made allegations of pain in locations where there were no IVs established and prior to any drugs being administered.” There have been 39 executions in the United States this year, all by lethal injection. Support for the death penalty among Americans has fallen to its lowest level in 55 years, according to a recent poll. Forty-nine percent of US adults are in favour of the death penalty for convicted murderers and 45 per cent are opposed, the Gallup poll found. AFP Kindly share this story:
